explain.say: Here is a place where some weather stations have gone years without recording any rain: the Atacama Desert in Chile. Scientists even test Mars rovers there! Look at the board. The question is why it almost never rains, and three dry forces work together.

explain.say: Second, a cold ocean current, the Humboldt Current, flows up the coast from the far south. It chills the air above it, and cold air near the sea will not rise to make rain clouds. So the coast gets fog, not rain. The Namib Desert in Africa is dry for the same reason!

faq.q: Why do deserts form where air sinks?
faq.a: Near 30 degrees north and south, air that rose at the Equator sinks back down. Sinking air warms up and can hold its moisture, so clouds rarely form. The Sahara, Arabian and Kalahari deserts lie in these belts.
asks: Why are many deserts near the Tropics?

faq.q: How does a cold current make a desert?
faq.a: A cold ocean current cools the air just above it. Cool air near the surface stays put instead of rising, so rain clouds cannot form, only fog. The Atacama has the Humboldt Current and the Namib has the Benguela Current.
asks: Why is the Namib Desert so dry?
How does a cold ocean current make a desert?

faq.a: When wet air meets mountains, it rises, cools and drops its rain on that side. By the time it sinks down the other side, it is dry. The dry land behind the mountains is called a rain shadow.
asks: Which side of a mountain gets the rain?

faq.q: How do people get water in the Atacama?
faq.a: From rivers fed by snow in the Andes, from wells, and from fog catchers: big mesh nets that catch tiny fog droplets, which drip into pipes and tanks.

faq.q: Is the Atacama really the driest place on Earth?
faq.a: It is the driest desert outside the polar regions. Arica, in the north, averages less than 1 mm of rain a year. Only parts of Antarctica, like the McMurdo Dry Valleys, are drier.
asks: How much rain does the Atacama get?

facts: Arica, in the Atacama, averages less than 1 mm of rain a year.
NASA has tested Mars rover instruments in the Atacama because its soil is so dry.
The cold Humboldt Current flows north along the coasts of Chile and Peru.
